name: Incentives
rule: People and institutions follow what's rewarded, not what's intended. Before assuming malice, check the incentives and what information people had.
plain: Show me how someone is paid, and I'll show you how they'll behave.

story.beat: To speed recovery, the council pays a bonus per kilogram of harvested greens. Harvests jump, and oxygen drops. The crew is picking plants young and heavy with water, before they've produced much oxygen. Nobody cheated; they did exactly what was paid for. You rewrite the bonus: pay per litre of oxygen measured at the dome's outlet.

examples.text: Dox is paid per visit, so appointments get shorter and more frequent. Nobody planned that.
Miners paid per tonne ignore safety checks. Adding a bonus for injury-free months changes behaviour within weeks.
Councillors elected every 6 months favour quick fixes over the 10-year oxygen plan.

realCase.title: The Hanoi rat bounty
realCase.text: French colonial authorities in Hanoi paid a bounty for each rat tail to fight plague. Officials soon saw tailless rats running the streets: people cut off tails and let the rats go on breeding. Some even farmed rats for the bounty.
realCase.source: Michael G. Vann, 'Of Rats, Rice, and Race', French Colonial History 4 (2003)

misuse: Assuming incentives explain everything and ignoring values, habits and identity. People also act from duty and pride, and poorly designed pay can crowd those out.
sources: Charlie Munger, 'The Psychology of Human Misjudgment' (1995)

predict.prompt: The council pays per kg of greens harvested. What happens to oxygen output?
options: It may fall as the crew harvests young, heavy plants early
predict.why: People optimise the paid metric, not the goal.

mcq.prompt: The Hanoi rat bounty backfired because…
options: tails were rewarded, not dead rats, so people bred rats
mcq.why: The reward measured tails, not fewer rats.

whichModel.prompt: A bank sets high sales targets; employees open millions of fake accounts.
whichModel.why: They followed the reward, not the intention.
